title: Graded-prefetch adaptive slab pacing for paged KV to reduce GPU page faults and tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a graded-prefetch, adaptive slab-pacing layer for the paged/blocked KV cache that reduces GPU page-fault stalls and smooths tail latency under mixed sequence-length workloads. This ticket captures the design and implementation tasks for a runtime component that applies paced, size-aware prefetching and host->device staging policies to keep hot segments resident while bounding peak GPU memory usage.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration with serving runtime: graded-prefetch scheduler activated when paged KV is enabled
P99 token-add latency reduced by >=15% on the mixed-seq benchmark compared to baseline without graded prefetch
Peak device memory variance reduced (stddev) by >=20% across 30-minute stress runs
No regression in throughput for short-sequence micro-batched workloads (within 3% of baseline)
Telemetry: new metrics (segment_prefetch_rate, staged_bytes, device_page_faults, prefetch_backpressure_seconds) emitted and visible in Console
implementation_notes: Introduce a graded prefetch priority: hot->warm->cold. Hot segments get async GPU memcpy immediately, warm segments are host-staged and copied with a lower-rate pacing window, cold segments are left on host until referenced

Slab-pacing: allocate prefetch budget as a function of recent token-affinity and batch-size histogram. Budget is represented as bytes per-second per-GPU and bounded by dynamic headroom estimation from device free memory and active kernel occupancy

Async copy strategy: use two CUDA streams per GPU (copy stream, compute stream) and overlap copies with KV query kernels. Implement copy coalescing for adjacent slab ranges to reduce PCIe/PCIEe overhead
Backpressure: when prefetch backlog grows > configurable thresholds, throttle new prefetches and inform the scheduler to trigger smaller batch-window fallbacks
Host-staged pooling: maintain a pinned-host slab cache for warm segments to avoid repeated pagefaults into pageable host memory; reuse pinned buffers to limit total pinned bytes
Eviction policy: add residency score combining recency, token affinity, and predicted next-token distance. Eviction prefers demoting large cold segments first to reduce fragmentation
Heuristics tuning: sequence-length aware thresholds (short/medium/long) and progressive aggression ramp on observed page-fault rates
Compatibility: fallback to existing slab allocator when GPU lacks async copy or pinned host memory support
APIs: add runtime flags enable_prefetch_pacing, prefetch_budget_bytes_per_sec, staging_pinned_bytes_limit for Dedicated and Private builds
test_plan: Unit tests for graded-priority queue, pacing token bucket, and eviction scoring
Integration tests in CI that simulate mixed-sequence distributions (80/15/5 short/medium/long) and assert P99 improvement
Synthetic stress runs to exercise oversubscription and verify graceful fallback path
Hardware regression matrics on p4d, a100, and a40 variants to confirm copy overlap benefits
Chaos test: simulate intermittent NVMM/PCIe slowdown and assert prefetch backpressure prevents catastrophic OOMs
metrics: prefetch_hit_ratio: fraction of lookups that found segment on-device after prefetch
experiment_results: Early devbench on a mixed-seq trace (avg seq 96 tokens, tails to 2048) showed device_page_faults drop ~38% and p99 generation latency drop of 18% with prefetch_budget tuned to 1.8GB/s on A100. Warm staging reduced repeated pagefault spikes in hot loops; however throughput dropped ~2.5% for tiny micro-batches until copy coalescing was added.
rollout_plan: Canary on hosted-api with 5% traffic pinned to runtime-1.22+prefetch (disable by config) for 48 hours
Monitor metrics and set automatic rollback if device_page_faults increase >10% or p99 latency regresses >5%
Gradual ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24 hour holds and manual sign-off
Dedicated/private: ship as opt-in flag in the console and document tuning recipes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive prefetch could saturate PCIe and harm throughput. Mitigation: token-bucket pacing and dynamic headroom sampling before copies.
Risk: Pinned host memory growth could reduce host-side performance. Mitigation: enforce pinned_bytes_limit and LRU demotion from pinned pool.
Risk: Fragmentation from demoting many small slabs. Mitigation: coalescing pass during low-load windows and prefer demoting large contiguous ranges first.
Risk: Behavior variance across GPU types. Mitigation: maintain per-GPU profiles and disable pacing where async copy benefit is negative.
